rules.name: all-equal middle-residue window rule (flat for n>=1, [s]^k for n=0)
rules.description_text: Domain: r>=4, k=len(a)>=3, all a_i equal to a, s = a mod r in [2, r-2]; n = floor(a/r). (1) If b <= kn+1, P is unimodal. (2) Otherwise let e = b-1-kn and K = k(s-1)+1-r(2+e). This does not depend on n. Let tau_t = Gamma_t - Gamma_{t-1} (indices mod r), where Gamma_t = number of k-tuples in {0,...,s-1}^k whose sum is congruent to t mod r. Equivalently, tau_t = (2/r) * sum_{j=1}^{r-1} sin(pi j/r) * (sin(pi j s/r)/sin(pi j/r))^k * sin(pi j (k(s-1)+1-2t)/r). If n>=1, let h_j = sum_{l>=0, lr<=j} C(j-lr+k-2, k-2) for j>=0, i.e. the coefficients of 1/((1-q)^(k-1)(1-q^r)). If n=0, let h_j be the power-series coefficients of [s]_q^k (1-q)/(1-q^r). In both cases h_j = 0 for j<0. Then P is unimodal iff tau_{m mod r} + h_{K-m} - h_m >= 0 for each of the r integers m with K/2 - r <= m < K/2. Only positions with tau_m < 0 can fail. Consequences: for n>=1, U = [1,kn+1] united with (kn+1+E_inf(r,s,k)), so U depends on n only through the shift F = kn. E_inf has the form {odd e <= E_odd} united with {even e <= E_even}, with E_odd < E_even. B* = kn+1+E_even, and U is either [1,B*] or [1,B*] minus {B*-1}.
rules.fit_range: 4<=r<=30, middle s in [2,r-2], 3<=k<=60, a<=100 (every n with n*r+s<=100), b from 1 to T6+2; ground truth was a full Thm-A scan validated against gt_big

numeric_claims.claim: The rule makes 0 errors on 4,824,541 (instance,b) pairs: r=4..8 with all n, r=9..30 with n in {0,1}, k=3..60, b<=T6+2. It also makes 0 errors on 5,315 random gt_big pairs with random n.
The rule makes 0 errors on 919,946 pairs from 63,684 instances with n>=2 (b in [F+1,T6+2]).
E(1) equals the flat set E_inf (exact window computation) for all 21,924 triples (r,s,k). With the proven sandwich this gives E(n) = E_inf for every n>=1 for these triples.
The flat formula also holds for n>=1 in all 97,556 full-scan instances. For n=0 it fails in 2,363 of 21,924 instances: E(0) is a proper subset of E_inf there.
Window Lemma sanity check on general (not all-equal) tuples: 0 disagreements with gt_big on 43,078 random (tuple,b) pairs.
Shape of E_inf over 21,924 triples: an interval in 15,072, empty in 6,304, a single hole at E_even-1 in 548, and no other shape. The n=0 sets also show no other shape.
No linear-floor (Beatty) law E_even/2 = floor(alpha k + gamma) fits exactly for 65 of the 378 (r,s) pairs. The best per-pair fit (756 real parameters in total) still mispredicts 113 (r,s,k) values.
The established bound T6 is not attained (B* != T6) in 93,462 of 119,480 instances.
numeric_claims.range: all generated data, r 4..30, k 3..60, a<=100

For n=1 versus flat, the per-position window signs agree in all 340,266 window values. The minimum slack ratio Phi_c/(Phi_c - Phi_g) is 1.956.
The rule reproduces Handelman's theorem (1+q)^k(1+q^r) unimodal iff k >= r^2-3, with 0 disagreements in 1,566 pairs.

numeric_claims.claim: Cyclic unimodality: tau_t >= 0 on the half period below D_s/2 at all 225,533 positions checked.

proofs.statement: Window Lemma, a sharpening of Thm A to r inequalities: for any palindromic, unimodal, nonnegative A (in particular any product of [a_i]_q), with g = A(1-q)/(1-q^r), tau its r-periodic tail and K = D+1-r(b+1), P = A[b]_{q^r} is unimodal iff tau_m + g_{K-m} - g_m >= 0 for the r integers m with K/2-r <= m < K/2.

Sandwich theorem for a = nr+s, s middle: E(0) is contained in E(1), which is contained in E(2), and so on, with E(n) = E_inf(r,s,k) for every n with 2(nr+s) > k(s-1)+1-r. Here E(n) = {e : kn+1+e in U}, and E_inf is defined by the window test with c = 1/((1-q)^(k-1)(1-q^r)) and tau from [s]^k. Combined with the exact computation E(1) = E_inf, this proves U([nr+s]^k) = [1,kn+1] united with (kn+1+E_inf) for all n>=1, for every 4<=r<=30, middle s, 3<=k<=60.
proofs.proof_file: /tmp/claude-0/qu/explore2/R2E5/proofs.txt (Lemmas 7-9, Theorem S, Computation C1, Theorem F)

proofs.statement: Parity structure of E_inf, for all r>=4, middle s, k>=3: e+2 in E_inf implies e in E_inf, and odd e in E_inf implies e+1 in E_inf. The second step uses a new cyclic-unimodality lemma for the residue sums of [s]^k. Hence E_inf = {odd e <= E_odd} united with {even e <= E_even}, with E_odd < E_even, and part (i) of Conjecture S2 holds for this family wherever E(n) = E_inf. Part (ii) is equivalent to E_odd >= E_even-3, which was checked for r<=30, k<=60.
Closed form: tau_t = (2/r) sum_{j=1}^{r-1} sin(pi j/r) sigma_j^k sin(pi j (k(s-1)+1-2t)/r), with sigma_j = sin(pi j s/r)/sin(pi j/r). In the window, the tau part depends on e only through its parity.

rules.name: C11: asymptotic excess clipped to the proved residue-only window
rules.description_text: If r divides some a_i: unimodal (C43). If b <= 1+F: unimodal (T1). If k < 3: not unimodal. Otherwise unimodal iff b <= 1+F+E_pred, where E_pred is built as follows. Let s_i = a_i mod r, S1 = sum(s_i-1), sigma1 = S1/k. Let L = (1/k) * max over j=1..r-1 of sum_i ln|sin(pi*j*s_i/r)/sin(pi*j/r)| (a term with a zero sine gives -infinity for that j). Let theta* be the root of H(t) = (1+t)ln(1+t) - t ln t = L, and lambda = ln(1+1/theta*). Set X = (S1 - 2*theta*k)/r - ln(k)/(r*lambda) (drop the log term if theta* = 0), and e0 = 2*floor((X - 0.5)/2). Window: tau_t = coefficients of (1-q)*prod_i [s_i]_q reduced mod q^r - 1, M = max_t tau_t; delta_n = sum over t>=0 with rt <= n+1 of C(n+1-rt+k-3, k-3) (0 for n < -1); n_lo = least n>=0 with delta_n >= M; n_hi = least integer n >= -r with 2r*delta_{n+r-1} >= M; E_lo = floor((S1+1-2r-2n_lo)/r), E_hi = floor((S1+1-2r-2n_hi)/r). lo = max(E_lo,0) rounded up to even, hi = E_hi rounded down to even. If lo <= hi, clip e0 into [lo,hi]. E_pred = max(e0,0). Claimed domain: k>=3, r divides no a_i, at least three a_i with a_i mod r in [2,r-2].
rules.fit_range: In-box fit set of 1600 instances (out/fit_1..4.jsonl): r in [4,30], k in [3,40] (up to 60 if all a_i are equal), a_i <= 100, r divides no a_i, at least 3 middle residues, b in [1, T6+2]. That is 195666 (instance,b) pairs. Hold-out out/hold_11,12.jsonl (800 instances, 102673 pairs): 37 pair errors in 24 instances.

rules.name: C3': pure closed-form asymptotic excess
rules.description_text: If r divides some a_i: unimodal. If b <= 1+F: unimodal. If k < 3: not unimodal. Otherwise unimodal iff b <= 1+F+E_pred, with E_pred = max(0, 2*floor((X - 0.5)/2)) and X = k*(sigma1 - 2*theta*)/r - ln(k)/(r*ln(1+1/theta*)). Here sigma1 = mean(s_i - 1), s_i = a_i mod r, L = (1/k) max_{1<=j<=r-1} sum_i ln|sin(pi j s_i/r)/sin(pi j/r)|, and theta* solves (1+t)ln(1+t) - t ln t = L. The rule uses only r, k and the residue multiset. Claimed domain: k>=3, r divides no a_i, at least three middle residues.
rules.fit_range: Same fit set as C11: 1600 instances, 195666 pairs, r 4..30, k 3..40 (60 if all equal), a_i <= 100. Fit errors are 93 pairs in 60 instances. Hold-out: 53 pairs in 32 instances.

Checks of the proved statements on the instances that meet their hypotheses. All 606 instances with a_min >= 2n_lo+2r have max(0,E_lo) <= E <= E_hi and no b >= F+2+E_hi in U. All 366 that also have a_min >= S1+2-r contain [1,F+1+E_lo] in U. All 495 with a_min >= 2n_+ + 2r satisfy the explicit window of Thm 2.

The explicit window [E_-,E_+], computed from (r,k,S1,L) only, and the sandwich [E_lo,E_hi] both contain E in 1592/1592 family cases. These cover 36 residue patterns with k from 3 to 40 (60 for a single residue). The explicit window has maximum width 5 and mean width 2.63.

For each family, the least-squares slope of E + kappa ln k against k (k = 6..60 or 6..40) matches the predicted leading constant c = (sigma1 - 2 theta*)/r to within 0.021, across all 26 families with c >= 0.05. rule_C11 makes 71 errors in 195666 fit pairs (49/1600 instances) and 37 in 102673 hold-out pairs (24/800). rule_C3 makes 93 fit errors (60 instances) and 53 hold-out errors (32 instances).

C3 (beta=-0.5, no clipping) predicts E exactly in 1500/1600 fit instances. Every miss is off by 2: 89 are too low and 11 too high. The share of wrong-E instances falls from 40/283 for k<=10 to 9/377 for k=31..40.

Leading constants for single-residue families: c(4,2)=0.1976, c(6,2)=0.0984, c(6,3)=0.2354, c(6,4)=0.4317, c(10,5)=0.2548, c(30,15)=0.2646. The log coefficient kappa = 1/(r ln(1+1/theta*)) is about 0.09-0.12 for middle residues.

Sanity check of Lemma 6 over 20000 random residue distributions with r <= 30 and positive middle mass: 0 < theta* < sigma1/2 holds every time, and the smallest observed (sigma1-2theta*)/sigma1 is 0.5435. On the grid x in (0,100], min of H(x) - ln(1+2x) is 0.0059 > 0.
The Lemma 5 width bound n_lo - n_hi < r + ln(2r)/ln R (and the matching bound on E_hi - E_lo) holds for all 2400 fit and hold-out residue vectors.

proofs.statement: Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 (sandwich). Let k>=3 and suppose r divides no a_i. Let M = max_t tau_t, where tau = (1-q)A(q) mod (q^r-1); M equals max|tau_t| by antisymmetry. Let delta_n = [q^{n+1}] 1/((1-q)^{k-2}(1-q^r)). Define n_lo = min{n>=0: delta_n >= M}, n_hi = min{n in Z: 2r delta_{n+r-1} >= M}, E_lo = floor((S1+1-2r-2n_lo)/r) and E_hi = floor((S1+1-2r-2n_hi)/r). If a_min >= 2n_lo+2r, then: max(0,E_lo) <= E = B*-1-F <= E_hi; no b >= F+2+E_hi is in U; and if also a_min >= S1+2-r, then [1,F+1+E_lo] is contained in U. Lemma 5 bounds the window: E_hi - E_lo < 3 + 2 ln(2r)/(r ln R), with R = (n_lo+k-3)/n_lo. The proof first reduces unimodality exactly to: g_{K-m} - g_m + tau_m >= 0 for -rb <= m <= (K-1)/2, where g = A/[r]_q and K = D+1-r(b+1).

Theorem 2 (explicit window from residue statistics). (2 sin(pi/r)/r) e^{L_k} <= M <= (2(r-1)/r) e^{L_k}, where L_k = max_j sum_i ln|sin(pi j s_i/r)/sin(pi j/r)|. Hence the window of Corollary 1 holds with n_lo and n_hi replaced by thresholds n_+ and n_- that depend only on (r, k, L_k).

Theorem 3 (growth order). Fix r and rational residue proportions with positive mass on middle residues, and let k -> infinity with exact counts. Let L = max_j sum_s p_s ln|sin(pi j s/r)/sin(pi j/r)|, theta* the root of (1+t)ln(1+t) - t ln t = L, lambda = ln(1+1/theta*), sigma1 = sum p_s (s-1), and c = (sigma1 - 2theta*)/r. Then for all a with these residues and a_min >= 2theta* k + ln k/lambda + C1: |E - (c k - ln k/(r lambda))| <= C2. The constants depend only on r and the proportions. Lemma 6 gives 0 < c < sigma1/r. So the excess is linear in k, never bounded and never superlinear, and E6 - E = (2theta* k + ln k/lambda)/r + O(1) -> infinity: the T6 bound is off by a linearly growing amount. If middle residues have density zero, E = S1/r + O(1) = E6 + O(1). The O(1) term oscillates and does not converge.

Lemma 6. For any residue distribution with sigma1 > 0: L < H(sigma1/2). L > 0 when the middle mass is positive. Proof uses |[s]_zeta| <= min(s,r-s), H(x) > ln(1+2x) for x > 0, and concavity of H (Jensen).

path_id: R2E7: explicit L0 and explicit U_inf (finite-state description) in the large-part regime

rules.name: B4-explicit window rule (proved)
rules.description_text: Let s_i = a_i mod r (none 0), S = sum s_i, k = len(a), K0 = S-k+1, F = sum floor(a_i/r). Domain: r divides no a_i, k>=1, min(a) >= L0 = max(1, floor((S-k+3-r)/2)). Let tau_t (t mod r) be the coefficients of (1-q)*prod_i [s_i]_q reduced mod q^r-1 (tau_t = sum of the coefficients in degrees congruent to t). Let w_n = coefficient of q^n in 1/((1-q)^(k-1)(1-q^r)), with w_n = 0 for n<0. Predict unimodal iff b <= F+1, or, with e = b-F and Delta = K0 - r(e+1): for every integer m with Delta/2 < m <= Delta/2 + r (r values), w_m - w_{Delta-m} >= tau_{m mod r}. (Outside the domain predict() returns True when r | some a_i, by C43; otherwise it applies the same test, but nothing is claimed there.) U_inf = {1} union {e>=2 : test holds}. It depends only on (r,k,S,tau) and is contained in [1, T] with T = 1+floor((K0-2mu)/r), mu = max{t: tau_t>0}.
rules.fit_range: r<=30, k<=40, a_i<=100, inside the domain; all b from 1 to F+floor(S/r)+4

rules.name: Two-chain explicit U_inf (proved, k>=2)
rules.description_text: Same domain as rule_B4 plus k>=2. T = 1+floor((K0-2mu)/r), Delta_e = K0-r(e+1). For a chain top c in {T, T-1}, let W = {m : Delta_c/2 < m <= Delta_c/2 + r}. For each m in W, let J(m) = least j>=0 with w_{m+jr} - w_{Delta_c-m+jr} >= tau_{m mod r}. Chain top value = c - 2*max_{m in W} J(m). This gives e_odd (from c=T, floored at 1) and e_even (from c=T-1, floored at 0). U_inf = {odd e <= e_odd} union {even e with 2 <= e <= e_even}. Predict unimodal iff b <= F+1 or b-F is in U_inf. This is equivalent to rule_B4 (Theorem 5).
rules.fit_range: r<=30, k in [2,40], a_i<=100, inside the domain

proofs.statement: Theorem 1 (window criterion, all r>=2, k>=1, a_i>=1, b>=1): with Delta = D+1-r(b+1), P is unimodal iff g_m - g_{Delta-m} >= tau_{m mod r} for the r integers m in (Delta/2, Delta/2+r], where g are the one-sided coefficients of A/[r]_q. Equivalently, P is unimodal iff it is weakly increasing on the last r steps before N/2. Each residue class of the differences is monotone on (D/2, N/2].

Theorem 2/3 (explicit L0): if r divides no a_i and min a_i >= floor(Delta/2)+r+1, then P is unimodal iff R_k(Delta). Hence for min a_i >= L0(r,s) = max(1, floor((S-k+3-r)/2)), U = [1,F+1] u {F+e : e>=2, R_k(K0-r(e+1))}. Here R_k uses only w = coefficients of 1/((1-q)^(k-1)(1-q^r)) and tau = (1-q)prod[s_i]_q mod q^r-1, so U_inf depends only on (r,k,S,tau).

Theorem 4 (universal necessity, any part sizes, k>=2, r divides no a_i): if P is unimodal then R_k(Delta) holds. So U(a) is contained in [1,F+1] u (F+U_inf(r, residues of the parts >=2)) for every a. Proof via the eps lemma: B-c >= 0 everywhere and nondecreasing up to (D+a_max+1)/2.

Theorem 5 (two-chain structure, k>=2): R_k(Delta) implies R_k(Delta+2r). So U_inf = {odd e <= e_odd} u {even e in [2,e_even]}, and each chain top equals c - 2*max_m J(m), with J(m) the least j such that w_{m+jr} - w_{Delta_c-m+jr} >= tau_m. In the large regime, b in U and b >= F+4 imply b-2 in U.
Theorem 6: R_k(Delta_e) fails for every e > T = 1+floor((S-k+1-2mu)/r), so U_inf is contained in [1, T6-F]. Combined with Theorem 4 this re-derives b <= T6 for all part sizes.

failure_report:
Partial negatives (the main rule did not fail):
(1) The proved L0 = max(1, floor((S-k+3-r)/2)) is safe but not sharp. For r<=7, k<=5 no failure was found at any L>=1. In targeted search, failures below L0 occurred for 11 of 271 multisets, at least 6 below L0. I found no residue-only formula for the sharp threshold: it depends on the actual parts, through how much the R inequalities have to spare against corrections at indices >= L.
(2) The three-shape conjecture is FALSE: 'U_inf is one of [1,T], [1,T]\{T-1}, [1,T-2] with T = T6-F'. It holds exhaustively for r<=13, k<=6 and other small ranges. For large k the gap T - e_odd reaches 4 and 6, e.g. r=10, k=40 with T=15 and U_inf=[1,11] (types_counter.py seed 1); it fails on 270 of 3000 random multisets, and rule_types has 130 b-errors out of 610085.
(3) The S2 shape for U_inf (e_even in {e_odd-1, e_odd-3}) is unproved; there are 0 counterexamples in all tested ranges. Theorem 5 reduces it to two inequalities, e_even < e_odd and e_even >= e_odd - 3.

rules.name: H1 (three middle residues)
rules.description_text: Domain: r>=4, r divides no a_i, and exactly three a_i have residue a_i mod r in [2,r-2]; every other a_i then has residue 1 or r-1. Compute tau = (1-q) * prod_i [a_i mod r]_q reduced mod (q^r - 1). This is a length-r integer vector with tau_t = Gamma_t - Gamma_{t-1}, and it depends only on the residues. Let mu = the largest j in [1,r-1] with tau_j > 0, or 0 if there is none; this is the mu of Theorem C. Let D = sum(a_i - 1), T6 = 1 + floor((D+1-2mu)/r) and s = (D+1) mod r. FIRE holds when tau_s <= -2 and s >= 2mu. Then B* = T6 - 2 if FIRE holds, otherwise B* = T6. Prediction: P is unimodal iff b <= B*, so U = [1,B*] is always an interval. B* - 1 - F is even and >= 0. Over all residue data with r<=30, FIRE occurs only when s = r-2 and tau_{r-2} = -2. FIRE depends only on (r, the middle residues, and the count of residue r-1 elements mod 2r), so it does not depend on F or on the sizes of the a_i.

proofs.statement: Take r>=4, r dividing no a_i, and exactly three a_i with residue in [2,r-2]. Let nm = #{a_i = -1 mod r}. If r<=30 and nm<=37, then U = [1,B*], where B* = T6 - 2*[tau_s<=-2 and s>=2mu] and s=(D+1) mod r. There is no restriction on the sizes of the a_i or on the number of a_i = 1 mod r. The proof uses: Lemma 1, the symmetry g_i = tau_i + g_{D+1-r-i}; Lemma 2, which shows by a general argument that the firing condition rules out every b>=T6-1; Lemma 3, peeling [x+r]_q[b]_{q^r} = [x+rb]_q + q^r[x]_q[b-1]_{q^r}, which gives U(a) containing [1,F] union (F+U(rho)); Lemma 4, B*(a)=B*(rho)+F; Lemma 5, an exact computation over the base family (r<=30, nm<=37, inside the fit box); and the established Thm A (g-form) and Thm C. Beyond this range (nm>=38 or r>=31) the base family is unverified and the rule is conjectural.

failure_report: Not a failure; the limits are as follows. The upper bound (Lemma 2 together with Thm C) and the reduction to residues (Lemmas 3 and 4) hold in general. The only gap is the lower bound for the base family (m1,m2,m3,(r-1)^nm) when nm>=38 or r>=31. Checking that by computation would need instances outside the fit box, so I did not do it. A structural argument for large nm, such as a peeling identity that removes pairs of (r-1) factors, was not found.
